finalText:
Evidence is sufficient. Here is the diagnosis.

---

## Diagnosis: Case c065 — Service `c065-svc` Unavailable

### Root Cause

The readiness probe in `deployment/c065-app` targets path **`/missing-healthz`** on port 8080, but the container (busybox running `httpd`) only serves content at `/` (specifically `/www/index.html`). The probe always gets a **404**, so the pod **never becomes Ready**.

Because the pod is perpetually NotReady, the Service has **zero endpoints** — clients have no backend to reach.

### Evidence

| Check | Finding |
|---|---|
| `svc/c065-svc` selector | `app: c065-app` — selector is correct |
| `svc/c065-svc` endpoints | **Empty** (no backend IPs) |
| Pod status | `0/1 READY`, status `Running` — container is up but probe fails |
| Readiness probe config | `httpGet: path: /missing-healthz, port: 8080` |
| Container command | `httpd -f -p 8080 -h /www` — only serves `/index.html` |
| Deployment conditions | `Available: False` (MinimumReplicasUnavailable), `Progressing: False` (ProgressDeadlineExceeded) |

### Impact / Scope

- **All traffic** to `c065-svc` (ClusterIP `172.17.213.21:80`) fails with connection refused / no backend.
- Single pod, single namespace — isolated to this workload only.

### Confidence

**High** — the readiness probe path is clearly misconfigured, directly causing the empty endpoints and service unavailability.

### Safe Remediation

Fix the readiness probe to match an actual route served by the container:

```yaml
# In the pod template, change:
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /missing-healthz   # ← wrong
    port: 8080
# To:
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /                  # ← correct (serves index.html)
    port: 8080
```

Alternatively, if the application is designed to serve a specific health endpoint, update the container command to handle that path. After the fix, run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/c065-app -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602` to apply the change.

## Diagnosis: Case c065 — Service `c065-svc` Unavailable

### Root Cause

The readiness probe in `deployment/c065-app` targets path **`/missing-healthz`** on port 8080, but the container (busybox running `httpd`) only serves content at `/` (specifically `/www/index.html`). The probe always gets a **404**, so the pod **never becomes Ready**.

Because the pod is perpetually NotReady, the Service has **zero endpoints** — clients have no backend to reach.

### Evidence

| Check | Finding |
|---|---|
| `svc/c065-svc` selector | `app: c065-app` — selector is correct |
| `svc/c065-svc` endpoints | **Empty** (no backend IPs) |
| Pod status | `0/1 READY`, status `Running` — container is up but probe fails |
| Readiness probe config | `httpGet: path: /missing-healthz, port: 8080` |
| Container command | `httpd -f -p 8080 -h /www` — only serves `/index.html` |
| Deployment conditions | `Available: False` (MinimumReplicasUnavailable), `Progressing: False` (ProgressDeadlineExceeded) |

### Impact / Scope

- **All traffic** to `c065-svc` (ClusterIP `172.17.213.21:80`) fails with connection refused / no backend.
- Single pod, single namespace — isolated to this workload only.

### Confidence

**High** — the readiness probe path is clearly misconfigured, directly causing the empty endpoints and service unavailability.

### Safe Remediation

Fix the readiness probe to match an actual route served by the container:

```yaml
# In the pod template, change:
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /missing-healthz   # ← wrong
    port: 8080
# To:
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /                  # ← correct (serves index.html)
    port: 8080
```

Alternatively, if the application is designed to serve a specific health endpoint, update the container command to handle that path. After the fix, run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/c065-app -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602` to apply the change.
